_about: The commandments taken up (plan 7.6b): commandments and sayings of the Law, Exodus to Deuteronomy, each beside the later passages that quote or repeat its words, in the prophets, the Psalms, the Gospels and the letters, with what is alike and what differs. Every quotation machine-checked against the Berean; rows chosen and drafted by Claude Opus from the passages the theme map cites, the Berean editors' quotation notes and a search of the whole Berean; widened by the completeness search; every Alike and Different line read by the nine-reader panel (Sonnet). Takes no interpretive stance. A cell [verse, words, "aside"] is off the subject and shown, with an asterisk, for its shared words.
columns_note: The Law & history: Genesis to Esther. Psalms & wisdom: Job to the Song of Solomon. The Prophets: Isaiah to Malachi.

rows.title: Love the LORD your God with all your heart

The Law & history: you shall love the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength
to love Him, to serve the LORD your God with all your heart and with all your soul
to love the LORD your God and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul
whether you love Him with all your heart and with all your soul
you will love Him with all your heart and with all your soul
to love the LORD your God
turned to the LORD with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength
to love the LORD your God
to love the LORD your God
Gospels & Acts: Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind
Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your mind and with all your strength
to love Him with all your heart and with all your understanding and with all your strength
Love the Lord your God with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your strength and with all your mind

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 6:5, 13:3 and 30:6, Matthew 22:37, Mark 12:30 and Luke 10:27 all call for love of God “with all your heart and with all your soul”; Deuteronomy 10:12 and 11:13 have the same words for serving Him.
rows.different: Deuteronomy 6:5 names heart, soul and “strength”; Matthew 22:37 has “mind” and no strength, Mark 12:30 and Luke 10:27 have all four, and the scribe in Mark 12:33 says “understanding”. Deuteronomy 11:1, 11:22, 30:16 and 30:20 and Joshua 23:11 have “love the LORD your God” with no heart or soul named; Joshua 22:5 puts “with all your heart and with all your soul” after “serve Him”. 2 Kings 23:25 says Josiah “turned to the LORD with all his heart and with all his soul and with all his strength”, “according to all the Law of Moses”.

rows.title: Love your neighbor as yourself

Gospels & Acts: to love your neighbor as yourself

rows.alike: Leviticus 19:18, Matthew 19:19, Matthew 22:39, Mark 12:31, Mark 12:33, Luke 10:27, Romans 13:9, Galatians 5:14 and James 2:8 all have “love your neighbor as yourself”, with a capital “Love” in some.
rows.different: Leviticus 19:34 says it of the foreigner: “love him as yourself”. Matthew 5:43 has “Love your neighbor” without “as yourself”, beside “Hate your enemy”. Matthew 22:39 calls it “the second” and “like it”; Romans 13:9 says the commandments “are summed up in this one decree”, Galatians 5:14 “The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree”, and James 2:8 calls it “the royal law”.

rows.title: Fear the LORD and keep His commandments

The Law & history: to fear Me and keep all My commandments always
fear the LORD your God all the days of your lives by keeping all His statutes and commandments
the LORD commanded us to observe all these statutes and to fear the LORD our God
you shall keep the commandments of the LORD your God, walking in His ways and fearing Him
to fear the LORD your God by walking in all His ways
fear Him. Keep His commandments and listen to His voice
learn to fear the LORD his God by carefully observing all the words of this instruction and these statutes
learn to fear the LORD your God and to follow carefully all the words of this law
Psalms & wisdom: Blessed is the man who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments
I am a friend to all who fear You, and to those who keep Your precepts
Fear God and keep His commandments, because this is the whole duty of man

rows.alike: Each sets fearing God beside His commandments, statutes, precepts or law, keeping or delighting in them: "fear Me and keep all My commandments" (Deuteronomy 5:29), "fear Him. Keep His commandments" (Deuteronomy 13:4), "who fears the LORD, who greatly delights in His commandments" (Psalm 112:1), "Fear God and keep His commandments" (Ecclesiastes 12:13).
rows.different: In Deuteronomy the fear is joined to doing: "by keeping" (6:2), "by walking in all His ways" (10:12) and "by carefully observing" (17:19), and 17:19 and 31:12 say "learn to fear"; Deuteronomy 5:29 is a wish, "If only they had such a heart". Psalm 112:1 calls such a man "Blessed", Psalm 119:63 is spoken by one who is "a friend" to them, and Ecclesiastes 12:13 gives it as "the conclusion of the matter" and "the whole duty of man".

rows.title: Making wise the simple

The Law & history: Observe them carefully, for this will show your wisdom and understanding in the sight of the peoples
Psalms & wisdom: the testimony of the LORD is trustworthy, making wise the simple
all who follow His precepts gain rich understanding
Your commandments make me wiser than my enemies
I have more insight than all my teachers, for Your testimonies are my meditation
I discern more than the elders, for I obey Your precepts
The letters: the Holy Scriptures, which are able to make you wise for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus

rows.alike: Each ties wisdom or understanding to the LORD's testimony, precepts or commandments, or to the Holy Scriptures: "this will show your wisdom and understanding" (Deuteronomy 4:6), "making wise the simple" (Psalm 19:7), "Your commandments make me wiser" (Psalm 119:98), "able to make you wise" (2 Timothy 3:15).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 4:6 says the peoples will see it: "Surely this great nation is a wise and understanding people." Psalm 119:98-100 measures it against others, "wiser than my enemies", "more insight than all my teachers", "more than the elders". Psalm 111:10 sets it beside "The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom". 2 Timothy 3:15 speaks of "the Holy Scriptures" and continues "for salvation through faith in Christ Jesus".

rows.title: The law given through Moses, ordained by angels

The Law & history: all the statutes that the LORD has given them through Moses
the commandments and ordinances that the LORD gave the Israelites through Moses
This is the law that Moses set before the Israelites

all the law that My servant Moses commanded you
the commandments of the LORD, which He had given their fathers through Moses

the Law, which the LORD had commanded through Moses

rows.alike: Each names Moses or angels: "given them through Moses" (Leviticus 10:11), "the law that Moses gave us" (Deuteronomy 33:4), "through Your servant Moses" (Nehemiah 9:14), "the law of My servant Moses" (Malachi 4:4), "the law was given through Moses" (John 1:17). Acts 7:53 has "the law ordained by angels", Galatians 3:19 "administered through angels", and Hebrews 2:2 "the message spoken by angels".
rows.different: John 1:17 adds "grace and truth came through Jesus Christ"; John 7:19 has "Yet not one of you keeps it" and Acts 7:53 "yet have not kept it", each said to hearers; Galatians 3:19 asks "Why then was the law given?" and adds "by a mediator"; Hebrews 2:2 has "if the message spoken by angels was binding"; Malachi 4:4 names "Horeb" and Acts 7:38 "Mount Sinai".

rows.title: Hear, O Israel: the LORD is One

The Law & history: Hear, O Israel: The LORD our God, the LORD is One
The Prophets: Did not one God create us?
there is no God but Me
Gospels & Acts: Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 6:4 says “the LORD is One”, and Mark 12:29 gives the same words; Mark 12:32, Galatians 3:20 and James 2:19 say “God is one”, and other letters “one God”. Isaiah 44:6 has “there is no God but Me”, as 1 Corinthians 8:4 has “there is no God but one”.
rows.different: Mark 12:29 keeps the opening “Hear, O Israel” and calls it “the most important”; the letters have only “one God” or “God is one”. James 2:19 adds “Even the demons believe that-and shudder.”

rows.title: Worship the LORD your God and serve Him only

The Law & history: Fear the LORD your God, serve Him only
You are to fear the LORD your God and serve Him
Gospels & Acts: Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only
Worship the Lord your God and serve Him only

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 6:13, 1 Samuel 7:3, Matthew 4:10 and Luke 4:8 all have “serve Him only”.
rows.different: Deuteronomy 6:13 begins “Fear the LORD your God”, and Deuteronomy 10:20 has “fear the LORD your God and serve Him”, without “only”; Matthew 4:10 and Luke 4:8 begin “Worship the Lord your God”, in Jesus' answer after “it is written” (Luke 4:8: “It is written”). In 1 Samuel 7:3 Samuel joins it to “put away the foreign gods”.

rows.title: Do not put the LORD your God to the test

The Law & history: Do not test the LORD your God as you tested Him at Massah

The letters: We should not test Christ, as some of them did
where your fathers tested and tried Me

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 6:16 says “Do not test the LORD your God”, and Matthew 4:7 and Luke 4:12 give it as “Do not put the Lord your God to the test”; Exodus 17 and the Psalms tell how the people “tested the LORD” or “tested God”.
rows.different: Deuteronomy 6:16 names the place, “at Massah”, and Psalm 95:9 and Hebrews 3:9 say “your fathers tested and tried Me”. Ahaz says “I will not test the LORD”; Malachi 3:15 has “they even test God and escape”, said of evildoers; Acts 5:9 has “test the Spirit of the Lord” and 1 Corinthians 10:9 “test Christ”.

rows.title: Man does not live on bread alone

The Law & history: man does not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of the LORD
Gospels & Acts: Man shall not live on bread alone, but on every word that comes from the mouth of God
Man shall not live on bread alone

rows.alike: All three say man does not “live on bread alone”.
rows.different: Deuteronomy 8:3 ends “from the mouth of the LORD” and Matthew 4:4 “from the mouth of God”; Luke 4:4 stops at “bread alone”. Deuteronomy 8:3 speaks of the manna; in Matthew and Luke Jesus answers with “It is written”.

rows.title: Keep the Sabbath day holy

The Law & history: Remember the Sabbath day by keeping it holy
Keep the Sabbath, for it is holy to you
Observe the Sabbath day by keeping it holy
to keep the Sabbath day holy
The Prophets: all who keep the Sabbath without profaning it

Gospels & Acts: they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment

rows.alike: The Law, Nehemiah and Jeremiah all speak of keeping “the Sabbath day” “holy”, and Exodus 31:16 and Deuteronomy 5:15 also speak of keeping the Sabbath; Ezekiel has “Keep My Sabbaths holy”.
rows.different: Exodus 20:8 begins “Remember” and Deuteronomy 5:12 “Observe”; Deuteronomy 5:15 gives the reason, “you were a slave in the land of Egypt”; Jeremiah 17:22 adds “just as I commanded your forefathers”. Luke 23:56 says “they rested on the Sabbath, according to the commandment”; in John 9:16 some of the Pharisees say of Jesus “He does not keep the Sabbath”.

rows.title: Honor your father and mother

The Law & history: Honor your father and mother, so that your days may be long in the land
Each of you must respect his mother and father

Gospels & Acts: he need not honor his father or mother with it
Honor your father and your mother
The letters: that it may go well with you and that you may have a long life on the earth

rows.alike: Exodus 20:12, Matthew 15:4 and Ephesians 6:2 have “Honor your father and mother”, Matthew 19:19, Mark 10:19 and Luke 18:20 “honor your father and mother”, and Deuteronomy 5:16 and Mark 7:10 “Honor your father and your mother”.
rows.different: Exodus 20:12 adds “so that your days may be long in the land”; Deuteronomy 5:16 adds “that it may go well with you”, and Ephesians 6:3 has “that it may go well with you and that you may have a long life on the earth”, after calling it “the first commandment with a promise”. Matthew 15:4 says “God said” and Mark 7:10 “Moses said”. In Malachi 1:6 the LORD of Hosts says “A son honors his father” and asks “if I am a father, where is My honor?”

rows.title: Anyone who curses his father or mother

The Law & history: Anyone who curses his father or mother must surely be put to death
If anyone curses his father or mother, he must be put to death
Psalms & wisdom: Whoever curses his father or mother, his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness

Gospels & Acts: Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death
Anyone who curses his father or mother must be put to death

rows.alike: Exodus 21:17, Leviticus 20:9, Proverbs 20:20, Matthew 15:4 and Mark 7:10 all speak of one who “curses his father or mother”.
rows.different: Leviticus 20:9, Matthew 15:4 and Mark 7:10 have “must be put to death”, and Exodus 21:17 “must surely be put to death”; Proverbs 20:20 has “his lamp will be extinguished in deepest darkness”. Matthew 15:4 sets it beside “Honor your father and mother” and Mark 7:10 beside “Honor your father and your mother”.

rows.title: You shall not murder

The Prophets: Will you steal and murder, commit adultery and perjury
murder and stealing, and adultery are rampant

rows.alike: Exodus 20:13 and Deuteronomy 5:17 say “You shall not murder”; the Gospels and letters give it as “Do not murder”.
rows.different: Matthew 5:21 adds “Anyone who murders will be subject to judgment”, said “to the ancients”. Jeremiah 7:9 and Hosea 4:2 name murder in one list with stealing and adultery. James 2:11 sets it beside “Do not commit adultery” as words of one speaker: “He who said”.

rows.title: You shall not commit adultery

The letters: You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery?

rows.alike: Exodus 20:14 and Deuteronomy 5:18 say “You shall not commit adultery”; the Gospels, Romans 13:9 and James 2:11 have “Do not commit adultery”.
rows.different: Matthew 5:27 introduces it with “You have heard that it was said”. Luke 18:20, Romans 13:9 and James 2:11 name adultery before murder; Matthew 19:18 and Mark 10:19, like Exodus 20:13-14, name murder first. Romans 2:22 has it in a question: “You who forbid adultery, do you commit adultery?”

rows.title: You shall not steal

The letters: You who preach against stealing, do you steal?
He who has been stealing must steal no longer

rows.alike: Exodus 20:15 and Deuteronomy 5:19 say “You shall not steal”; the Gospels and Romans 13:9 have “do not steal”.
rows.different: Leviticus 19:11 sets “You must not steal” beside “You must not lie or deceive one another”. Romans 2:21 asks “You who preach against stealing, do you steal?”, and Ephesians 4:28 adds “but must work, doing good with his own hands”.

rows.title: You shall not bear false witness

You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor
If a false witness testifies against someone

The letters: we are also exposed as false witnesses about God

rows.alike: Exodus 20:16 and Deuteronomy 5:20 say “You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor”, and Proverbs 25:18 speaks of “a man who bears false witness against his neighbor”.
rows.different: The Gospel lists have “do not bear false witness” without “against your neighbor”. Proverbs 19:5 and 19:9 have “A false witness will not go unpunished”. Matthew 26:60, Mark 14:56 and Acts 6:13 tell of false witnesses, Mark 14:56 “against Jesus”; 1 Corinthians 15:15 has “false witnesses about God”.

rows.title: You shall not covet

rows.different: Exodus 20:17 names “your neighbor's house” first and Deuteronomy 5:21 “your neighbor's wife”; Romans gives only “Do not covet”. Deuteronomy 7:25 and Joshua 7:21 speak of silver and gold, Micah 2:2 of fields, and Acts 20:33 has “I have not coveted anyone's silver or gold or clothing”.

rows.title: Be holy, because I am holy

The Law & history: be holy, because I am holy

rows.different: Leviticus 19:2 is said to “the whole congregation of Israel”, and Leviticus 11:45 joins it to “who brought you up out of the land of Egypt”. 1 Peter 1:15 has “so be holy in all you do”, and 1:16 gives the words with “for it is written”. Leviticus 21:8 says “He shall be holy to you, because I the LORD am holy”, of one who “presents the food of your God”.

rows.title: Eye for eye, tooth for tooth

rows.alike: All four have “eye for eye” and “tooth for tooth”.
rows.different: Exodus 21:24 goes on “hand for hand, foot for foot”, Leviticus 24:20 begins “fracture for fracture”, and Deuteronomy 19:21 begins “life for life” after “You must show no pity”. Matthew 5:38 gives only the eye and the tooth, after “You have heard that it was said”.

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 23:21 says “If you make a vow to the LORD your God, do not be slow to keep it”, and Ecclesiastes 5:4 “When you make a vow to God, do not delay in fulfilling it”; Psalm 76:11 and Matthew 5:33 have “fulfill your vows”.
rows.different: Numbers 30:2 says “he must not break his word”, Matthew 5:33 “Do not break your oath”, said “to the ancients”. Psalms 22, 61, 66 and 116 speak in the first person: “I will fulfill my vows”. Ecclesiastes 5:5 adds “It is better not to vow”.

rows.title: Do not curse the ruler of your people

rows.alike: Exodus 22:28 and Acts 23:5 both speak of “the ruler of your people”; Ecclesiastes 10:20 has “Do not curse the king”.
rows.different: Exodus 22:28 says “curse” and joins it to “You must not blaspheme God”; Acts 23:5 says “speak evil about”, given by Paul with “it is written” after “I was not aware that he was the high priest”. Ecclesiastes 10:20 says “the king” and adds “even in your thoughts”.

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 24:1, Matthew 19:7 and Mark 10:4 all have a “certificate of divorce” and “send her away”.
rows.different: Deuteronomy 24:1 says “he may write her”; in Matthew 19:7 the questioners ask “did Moses order”, in Mark 10:4 they answer “Moses permitted”, and Matthew 5:31 has “must give her”. The letters: Cursed is everyone who is hung on a tree
He Himself bore our sins in His body on the tree

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 21:23 and Galatians 3:13 both have “hung on a tree” with a curse; Acts 5:30 and 10:39 say “hanging Him on a tree”. Deuteronomy 21:23 says the body must not be left “overnight”, and in Joshua 8:29 the body is taken down “at sunset”.
rows.different: Deuteronomy 21:23 says “under God's curse” and Galatians 3:13 “Cursed is everyone”, after “Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law by becoming a curse for us”. Acts 5:30 and 10:39 do not speak of a curse, and 1 Peter 2:24 says “bore our sins in His body on the tree”.

rows.title: Fathers not put to death for their children

The Law & history: Fathers shall not be put to death for their children, nor children for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin
Fathers must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin
Fathers must not be put to death for their children, and children must not be put to death for their fathers; each is to die for his own sin
The Prophets: each will die for his own iniquity
he will die for his own iniquity
A son will not bear the iniquity of his father, and a father will not bear the iniquity of his son

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 24:16, 2 Kings 14:6 and 2 Chronicles 25:4 end “each is to die for his own sin”, and Jeremiah 31:30 has “each will die for his own iniquity”.
rows.different: 2 Kings 14:6 and 2 Chronicles 25:4 give the words as “what is written”, where “the LORD commanded”, as the reason “he did not put the sons of the murderers to death” (2 Kings) and “he did not put their sons to death” (2 Chronicles). Jeremiah 31:30 and Ezekiel 18:18 say “iniquity” for “sin”, and Ezekiel 18:20 speaks of a son and a father who “will not bear the iniquity” of the other.

rows.title: Vengeance is Mine; I will repay

The Law & history: Vengeance is Mine; I will repay
The letters: Vengeance is Mine; I will repay, says the Lord
Vengeance is Mine; I will repay

rows.alike: All three have “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay”.
rows.different: In Deuteronomy 32:35 the words go on “In due time their foot will slip”. Romans 12:19 adds “says the Lord” and sets them after “Do not avenge yourselves, beloved, but leave room for God's wrath”; Hebrews 10:30 has “we know Him who said” and pairs them with “The Lord will judge His people”.

rows.title: The LORD will vindicate His people

The Law & history: the LORD will vindicate His people and have compassion on His servants
Psalms & wisdom: the LORD will vindicate His people and will have compassion on His servants
that He may judge His people
The letters: The Lord will judge His people

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 32:36 and Psalm 135:14 have the same words: “the LORD will vindicate His people” and “have compassion on His servants”.
rows.different: Deuteronomy 32:36 and Psalm 135:14 have “vindicate His people”; Hebrews 10:30 has “The Lord will judge His people”, set beside “Vengeance is Mine; I will repay”, and Psalm 50:4 has “that He may judge His people”.

rows.title: He will never leave you nor forsake you

The Law & history: He will never leave you nor forsake you
He will never leave you nor forsake you
I will never leave you nor forsake you
May He never leave us or forsake us
He will neither fail you nor forsake you
Psalms & wisdom: do not leave me or forsake me, O God of my salvation
The letters: Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you

rows.alike: Deuteronomy 31:6 and 31:8 have “He will never leave you nor forsake you”, Joshua 1:5 “I will never leave you nor forsake you”, and Hebrews 13:5 “Never will I leave you, never will I forsake you”.
rows.different: In Deuteronomy 31:6 and 31:8 “He” is said of the LORD; in Joshua 1:5 it is “I”, as in “As I was with Moses”, and Hebrews 13:5 gives the “I” form with “God has said”, beside “be content with what you have”. 1 Kings 8:57 has “May He never leave us or forsake us”, Psalm 27:9 “do not leave me or forsake me, O God of my salvation”, and 1 Chronicles 28:20 “He will neither fail you nor forsake you”.

rows.title: Fulfilling the law

Gospels & Acts: I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them
Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me in the Law of Moses, the Prophets, and the Psalms
this is to fulfill what is written in their Law
The letters: so that the righteous standard of the law might be fulfilled in us
he who loves his neighbor has fulfilled the law
love is the fulfillment of the law
The entire law is fulfilled in a single decree
Carry one another's burdens, and in this way you will fulfill the law of Christ
If you really fulfill the royal law stated in Scripture

rows.alike: Each joins "fulfill" to the law: "to fulfill them" (Matthew 5:17, of "the Law or the Prophets"), "has fulfilled the law" (Romans 13:8), "the fulfillment of the law" (Romans 13:10), "The entire law is fulfilled" (Galatians 5:14), "fulfill the law of Christ" (Galatians 6:2), "fulfill the royal law" (James 2:8).
rows.different: Romans 13:8, 13:10, Galatians 5:14 and James 2:8 join it to the neighbor ("he who loves his neighbor", "Love does no wrong to its neighbor", "Love your neighbor as yourself"); Galatians 6:2 to "Carry one another's burdens"; Romans 8:4 has "fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit"; Matthew 5:17 is Jesus saying "I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them". Luke 24:44 and John 15:25 use the words of what is written: "Everything must be fulfilled that is written about Me" and "to fulfill what is written in their Law".

rows.title: The Law of the LORD is perfect

Psalms & wisdom: The Law of the LORD is perfect, reviving the soul
I have seen a limit to all perfection, but Your commandment is without limit
The letters: for the law made nothing perfect
It can never, by the same sacrifices offered year after year, make perfect those who draw near to worship

rows.alike: Psalm 19:7 and James 1:25 both join "perfect" to the law: "The Law of the LORD is perfect" and "the perfect law of freedom". Hebrews 7:19 and 10:1 join the same two words, and Psalm 119:96 sets "Your commandment" beside "perfection".
rows.different: Psalm 19:7 adds "reviving the soul", and James 1:25 "of freedom" and "the one who looks intently into" it. Hebrews 7:19 has "the law made nothing perfect" and Hebrews 10:1 "It can never, by the same sacrifices offered year after year, make perfect those who draw near"; Psalm 119:96 has "I have seen a limit to all perfection, but Your commandment is without limit."

rows.title: The commandment is holy, righteous, and good

The Law & history: righteous statutes and ordinances like this entire law
just ordinances, true laws, and good statutes and commandments
Psalms & wisdom: the judgments of the LORD are true, being altogether righteous
The testimonies You have laid down are righteous
The Prophets: I also gave them over to statutes that were not good
The letters: the law is holy, and the commandment is holy, righteous, and good
the law is good, if one uses it legitimately
Revelation: true and just are Your judgments
His judgments are true and just

rows.alike: The same few words are said of the law and of its statutes, judgments, ordinances and commandments: "righteous" (Deuteronomy 4:8; Psalm 19:9; Psalm 119:75, 138, 172; Romans 7:12), "true" (Nehemiah 9:13; Psalm 19:9; Psalm 119:142, 151) and "good" (Nehemiah 9:13; Psalm 119:39; Romans 7:12, 16; 1 Timothy 1:8).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 4:8 asks "what nation is great enough" to have "righteous statutes and ordinances like this entire law"; Nehemiah 9:13 says "You gave them"; Psalm 119 speaks to God ("Your judgments", "Your law"), while Psalm 19:9 says "the judgments of the LORD". Romans 7:12 adds "holy" and 1 Timothy 1:8 "if one uses it legitimately". Ezekiel 20:25 has "I also gave them over to statutes that were not good".

rows.title: My delight is in Your law

Psalms & wisdom: his delight is in the Law of the LORD
I delight to do Your will, O my God
I will delight in Your statutes
Your testimonies are indeed my delight
Direct me in the path of Your commandments, for there I find delight
I delight in Your commandments because I love them
If Your law had not been my delight, then I would have perished in my affliction
The Prophets: Your words became my joy and my heart's delight
if you call the Sabbath a delight
The letters: For in my inner being I delight in God's law

rows.alike: Each calls the law or God's words a delight, or says the speaker delights in them: "his delight is in the Law of the LORD" (Psalm 1:2), "I delight in Your law" (Psalm 119:70), "my heart's delight" (Jeremiah 15:16), "I delight in God's law" (Romans 7:22).
rows.different: Psalm 1:2 speaks of one man ("his delight"); Psalm 119, Jeremiah 15:16 and Romans 7:22 speak in the first person. Psalm 119 varies the word: "Your statutes", "Your testimonies", "Your commandments", "Your law"; Jeremiah 15:16 has "Your words" and "I ate them", Romans 7:22 adds "in my inner being", and Psalm 40:8 has "I delight to do Your will". Isaiah 58:13 uses the word of the Sabbath: "call the Sabbath a delight".

rows.title: Meditate on it day and night

The Law & history: This Book of the Law must not depart from your mouth; meditate on it day and night
Psalms & wisdom: on His law he meditates day and night
I will meditate on Your precepts
Your servant meditates on Your statutes
I will meditate on Your precepts
Oh, how I love Your law! All day long it is my meditation
My eyes anticipate the watches of night, that I may meditate on Your word

rows.alike: Joshua 1:8 and Psalm 1:2 share meditating on the law "day and night": "meditate on it day and night" and "on His law he meditates day and night". Psalm 119 has "All day long it is my meditation" and "the watches of night, that I may meditate on Your word".
rows.different: Joshua 1:8 is a command to Joshua, naming "This Book of the Law", adding "must not depart from your mouth" and "so that you may be careful to do everything written in it". Psalm 1:2 speaks of one man ("he meditates"); Psalm 119 speaks to God of "Your precepts", "Your statutes", "Your law" and "Your word".

rows.title: The law in the heart

The Law & history: These words I am commanding you today are to be upon your hearts
Fix these words of mine in your hearts and minds
the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may obey it
Psalms & wisdom: Receive instruction from His mouth, and lay up His words in your heart
The law of his God is in his heart
Your law is within my heart
I have hidden Your word in my heart
let your heart keep my commandments
write them on the tablet of your heart
Never let loving devotion or faithfulness leave you; bind them around your neck, write them on the tablet of your heart
The Prophets: you people with My law in your hearts
The letters: the work of the law is written on their hearts
The word is near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart

rows.alike: Each puts a law, words or commandments in the heart or hearts, or says "the work of the law" is there: "upon your hearts" (Deuteronomy 6:6), "in your mouth and in your heart" (Deuteronomy 30:14; Romans 10:8), "The law of his God is in his heart" (Psalm 37:31), "Your law is within my heart" (Psalm 40:8), "My law in your hearts" (Isaiah 51:7), "written on their hearts" (Romans 2:15).
rows.different: Deuteronomy 6:6 and 11:18, Job 22:22 and Proverbs tell the hearer to put it there ("Fix these words of mine in your hearts and minds", "lay up His words in your heart", "write them on the tablet of your heart"); Psalms 37:31 and 40:8 and Isaiah 51:7 say it is there; Psalm 119:11 says "I have hidden Your word in my heart"; Deuteronomy 30:14 says "the word is very near you; it is in your mouth and in your heart, so that you may obey it". Romans 2:15 has "the work of the law" and adds "their consciences also bearing witness"; Romans 10:8 adds "that is, the word of faith we are proclaiming".

rows.title: Not hearers only, but doers

The Prophets: Who will listen and obey hereafter?
hear your words; but they do not put them into practice
They hear your words but do not put them into practice
Gospels & Acts: everyone who hears these words of Mine and acts on them
everyone who hears these words of Mine and does not act on them
hears My words and acts on them
the one who hears My words and does not act on them
those who hear the word of God and carry it out
Blessed rather are those who hear the word of God and obey it
anyone who hears My words and does not keep them
The letters: it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous
Be doers of the word, and not hearers only
anyone who hears the word but does not carry it out
not being a forgetful hearer, but an effective doer
Revelation: blessed are those who hear and obey what is written in it

rows.alike: Each sets hearing beside doing: "we will listen and obey" (Deuteronomy 5:27), "Who will listen and obey hereafter?" (Isaiah 42:23), "hears these words of Mine and acts on them" (Matthew 7:24), "hear the word of God and carry it out" (Luke 8:21), "the doers of the law" (Romans 2:13), "Be doers of the word, and not hearers only" (James 1:22), "hear and obey" (Revelation 1:3).
rows.different: What is heard differs: "all that the LORD our God says" (Deuteronomy 5:27), "your words" said to Ezekiel, "these words of Mine" (Matthew 7:24), "the word of God" (Luke 8:21; 11:28), "the law" (Romans 2:13), "the word" (James 1:22), "the words of this prophecy" (Revelation 1:3). Deuteronomy 5:27 is the people's promise and Ezekiel 33:31-32 says "they do not put them into practice"; Romans 2:13 adds "will be declared righteous" and James 1:25 "he will be blessed in what he does".

rows.title: Abolish, nullify, set aside

Gospels & Acts: Do not think that I have come to abolish the Law or the Prophets. I have not come to abolish them
not a single jot, not a stroke of a pen, will disappear from the Law until everything is accomplished
it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away than for a single stroke of a pen to drop out of the Law
Thus you nullify the word of God for the sake of your tradition
You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition
Thus you nullify the word of God by the tradition you have handed down
The letters: Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith? Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law.
by abolishing in His flesh the law of commandments and decrees
the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless
does not revoke the covenant previously established by God, so as to nullify the promise
I do not set aside the grace of God

rows.alike: Each speaks of abolishing, nullifying or setting aside the law, a commandment, or the word of God: "to abolish the Law or the Prophets" (Matthew 5:17), "nullify the word of God" (Matthew 15:6; Mark 7:13), "set aside the command of God" (Mark 7:9), "nullify the law" (Romans 3:31), "abolishing in His flesh the law of commandments and decrees" (Ephesians 2:15), "the former commandment is set aside" (Hebrews 7:18). Matthew 5:18 and Luke 16:17 share "a stroke of a pen", "heaven and earth" and "the Law".
rows.different: In Matthew 5:17 Jesus says "I have not come to abolish them, but to fulfill them". In Matthew 15:6 and Mark 7:13 He says "Thus you nullify the word of God", "for the sake of your tradition" (Matthew 15:6) and "by the tradition you have handed down" (Mark 7:13); in Mark 7:9 "You neatly set aside the command of God to maintain your own tradition." Romans 3:31 asks "Do we, then, nullify the law by this faith?" and answers "Certainly not! Instead, we uphold the law." Ephesians 2:15 has "by abolishing in His flesh", and Hebrews 7:18 "because it was weak and useless". Matthew 5:18 has "until everything is accomplished", Luke 16:17 "it is easier for heaven and earth to pass away".

rows.title: Justified before God

Psalms & wisdom: how can a mortal be righteous before God?
Gospels & Acts: everyone who believes is justified from everything from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses
The letters: it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous before God, but it is the doers of the law who will be declared righteous
no one will be justified in His sight by works of the law
a man is justified by faith apart from works of the law
If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God
a man is not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ
no one is justified before God by the law
the law became our guardian to lead us to Christ, that we might be justified by faith
You who are trying to be justified by the law have been severed from Christ
Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did
a man is justified by his deeds and not by faith alone
was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions

rows.alike: Each speaks of being justified or righteous. Job 9:2 and Romans 2:13 both have "righteous before God"; Galatians 3:11 has "justified before God" and Romans 3:20 "justified in His sight". Romans 3:28 and James 2:24 both have "a man is justified by", and Galatians 2:16 has "a man is not justified by".
rows.different: Job 9:2 asks a question and names neither the law nor faith. Acts 13:39 has "everyone who believes is justified". Romans 2:13 has "the doers of the law who will be declared righteous"; Romans 3:20 "by works of the law"; Romans 3:28 "by faith apart from works of the law"; Romans 4:2 "If Abraham was indeed justified by works, he had something to boast about, but not before God". Galatians 2:16 has "not justified by works of the law, but by faith in Jesus Christ". James 2:21 asks "Was not our father Abraham justified by what he did", James 2:24 has "by his deeds and not by faith alone", and James 2:25 asks "was not even Rahab the prostitute justified by her actions".
